t: Palindrome Rearrangement Queries — Mismatch Positions and Multiset Matching
o: For s to become a palindrome, each left-half index i must pair with its mirror n-1-i. A query makes two intervals rearrangeable: [a,b] in the left half and [c,d] in the right half, whose mirror images [n-1-d, n-1-c] and [n-1-b, n-1-a] also live in the left half. Two conditions arise: (1) every originally mismatched pair must touch at least one editable interval — equivalently, no mismatch lies outside the union U = [a,b] ∪ [n-1-d, n-1-c]; (2) the multiset of characters at left positions in U must equal the multiset at their mirror positions, checkable per character with prefix counts and inclusion–exclusion over interval intersections. All examples confirm: e.g. 'abbcdecbba' fails because the mismatch at pair (4,5) is untouched.
k: Editable left-half coverage is the union of [a,b] and the mirrored right interval [n-1-d, n-1-c]; all mismatches must fall inside it.
Multiset equality over a union of two intervals is computed per character via prefix counts minus the intersection — 26 checks per query.

a.n: Approach 1: Prefix counts + sorted mismatch list
a.i: Precompute 26 prefix-count arrays and the sorted list of left-half mismatch positions. Per query: binary-search that no mismatch lies outside the union, then compare per-character multiset counts on the left union versus the right union (mirror images), subtracting interval-intersection overlaps.
s: Build pref[c][i] prefix counts and mm = sorted mismatched left indices.
Condition A: zero mismatches in [0, min(a,n-1-d)-1] and [max(b,n-1-c)+1, m-1].
Condition B: for each character, count over [a,b] ∪ [l2a,l2b] equals count over [n-1-b,n-1-a] ∪ [c,d], with intersections subtracted.
a.t: O((n + q) · 26) — prefix construction plus 26 character comparisons and O(log n) binary searches per query

w: The decomposition into 'untouched pairs must already match' plus 'editable pairs must have matching multisets' is the whole problem; everything else is bookkeeping. Pitfalls: mirroring intervals correctly ([c,d] maps to [n-1-d, n-1-c]), clamping empty intersections, and remembering both rearrangeable substrings can overlap their own mirrors. Follow-up: allow swaps between the two substrings, or answer queries after point updates to s.
